, its fork of Pilot, in the servers. So Wolf stands on two grounds, and each idea below says which one it is for:
Dokos runs Central, Atlas, Cargo, Datum and Beacon. It holds the signing keys, the ClickHouse passwords, Desk on every application, and the script that builds the images

Only what is on the server counts: its files, its logs, Pilot's webhooks

No Frappe Cloud v2 application reads the inside of a bench. Central has no log, no per-site error and no security signal of any kind. Datum receives eight metrics and update events from a customer server. Beacon ignores a single failing site by design. Atlas sees a machine from its edge.

So on a customer's server the Wolf Agent is the only collector of: per-site 5xx, Frappe tracebacks, scheduler and worker failures, Frappe logins and role changes, SSH and sudo, attacks seen in nginx, file integrity, outbound connections. That is the ground
